text:
morgan: Quick check-in on rollout telemetry field contracts — want to lock a minimal schema so integrators (console/metrics/ops) don't break when we add fields.
tara: +1, saw a couple of surprises yesterday where new rollout hints caused the metrics pipeline to drop rows.
devon: can you sketch the minimal set you had in mind?
morgan: thinking required: rollout_id, model_tag, effective_time, stage (canary/stable/retired). optional: hints[], affinity_weight, origin (ui/cli/automation).
anya: also need an explicit tombstone flag vs soft-retire. we've been overloading stage=retired which made client code messy.
tara: +1 for tombstone boolean. If true, clients should stop resolving pins but keep telemetry for auditing.
devon: what about backward compat? older SDKs will only expect stage; we should encode tombstone as stage=retired + tombstone=true. clients that ignore tombstone still see retired — ok?
morgan: agreed. fallback rule: clients may ignore unknown fields; tombstone must be discoverable from stage OR tombstone flag.
infra-bot: note: metrics pipeline schema v2 will reject unknown top-level fields unless explicitly whitelisted.
tara: so we have two options: 1) whitelist new telemetry fields and version the pipeline or 2) keep all new stuff under a single opaque map e.g. metadata.extra that pipelines can ignore.
anya: I prefer metadata.extra because it reduces churn in downstream schemas. then we can iterate freely on hints.
devon: ok but we still need typed fields for important behaviors: tombstone, origin, affinity_weight. those shouldn't be opaque.
morgan: proposal: top-level required fields = [rollout_id, model_tag, effective_time, stage]. Controlled fields (typed, optional) = [tombstone, origin, affinity_weight, hints_v1]. All other extras go into metadata.extra (map).
tara: sounds reasonable. can we agree on names and types? devon and anya — quick thumbs? :thumbsup:
devon: :thumbsup: — tombstone: boolean, origin: enum(ui,cli,api,auto), affinity_weight: integer 0-100. hints_v1: array of strings for now.
anya: :thumbsup: also add deprecated_at: nullable timestamp for soft-retire timelines.
morgan: adding sample minimal schema for ops (we can evolve):
```json
{
  "rollout_id": "string",
  "model_tag": "string",
  "effective_time": "iso8601 string",
  "stage": "enum(canary,stable,retired)",
  "tombstone": "boolean (optional)",
  "origin": "enum(ui,cli,api,automation) (optional)",
  "affinity_weight": "int 0-100 (optional)",
  "deprecated_at": "iso8601 (nullable, optional)",
  "metadata": {
    "extra": "map<string,any> (opaque)"
  }
}
```
tara: nice. question: how do we handle model version aliasing? e.g., model_tag can be alias like @stable-3, we need canonical_id somewhere for reconciliations.
morgan: good call — add canonical_model_id (optional) for deterministic reconciliation. clients should prefer canonical if present.
devon: ops concern: when rolling back, we need to signal affinity changes without changing rollout_id. maybe support an incrementing rollout_epoch int?
anya: yes add rollout_epoch: int (default 0) so we can increment semantics without new ids.
tara: summary of agreed fields (finalize in RFC): required: rollout_id, model_tag, effective_time, stage; typed optional: tombstone, origin, affinity_weight, deprecated_at, canonical_model_id, rollout_epoch; opaque: metadata.extra.
morgan: I'll update the draft RFC and add migration notes for metrics whitelist and client SDKs. plan: land schema in control-plane, cut metrics whitelist and release SDK stubs next week.
devon: also add a regen script for sample events so metrics team can sanity check.
anya: thanks. leaving a follow-up: we should document client fallback heuristics (ignore unknowns, use canonical_id if available, treat tombstone as strong signal).
infra-bot: action created: #1234 (control-plane/schema) assigned to morgan, due 3d.
morgan: sweet. If no objections I'll push the patch for the schema file tomorrow morning.
tara: no objections from me. thanks!
